HARD v1 Table 1 static HARD-Both ASRs 12.1/1.3/13.9/7.4 conflict with introduction/adjacent prose 15.4/1.0/6.7/10.2; appendix MC/SP UA 86.3/92.0 conflicts with Table 1 85.9/95.1. Table 3's GLM-5.2 memory-contamination row independently matches Table 1 on ASR=13.9 and UA=85.9, partially favoring that lineage without resolving all static cells. LPA 4.8 vs 12.1 and GPT-5.5 UA=7.2 are verified within their exact five-round regimes.

Table 4 values are verified and w/o CBR is explicitly episodic-memory-disabled, yet it rises 78.65→84.47 (+5.82pp), slightly more than the two CBR arms. The paper-era repository lacks the five-iteration experiment harness/CBR implementation and v2 does not specify the no-CBR inter-iteration operator, seeds/order, retry/cumulative accounting or raw manifests. Therefore same-iteration CBR separation is usable, but the shared upward iteration slope is causally unidentified and must not be attributed specifically to memory learning.

ViT-t/ImageNet subset-size results and reward-std declines are verified: fullset 65.23/71.09/73.47/75.34 for 1/1024→1/128 and declines 0.06/0.06/0.08/0.13. The 0.2/0.1 thresholds are empirical Rocket diagnostics, not general constants or a direct rank-correlation test. The approximately-80x claim is a separate ResNet-18/ImageNet EFLOPs comparison, not direct wall-clock speedup. No raw ImageNet subset/full paired-rank artifact is explicitly listed in the released data inventory.

The v4 formal theorem gives interval tracking error <=(Lambda+2eta)/(eta L), so O(1/sqrt(T)) applies to the full horizon with eta=T^-1/2 and constant Lambda, not uniformly to every short interval. Theorem 2 verifies stochastic O((Cmax/(1-phi))*sqrt(nT log(nT))) expected cost regret. Projection can hide linear validity debt; guaranteed-success/failure boundary arms are proof-critical structural assumptions for the presented algorithm.

The paper verifies a random pooled manual sample of n=50 with estimated ~12% heuristic-judge misclassification, mostly ambiguous-redirection false negatives, and no false positives observed. It does not report class denominators/confusion matrix, confidence interval, inter-rater/annotation protocol or controlled corruption sweep. Devstral uses 20 generations. A paper/code fitness-scale provenance inconsistency remains: method text uses 1.0 compliance while results/linked HeuristicJudge use a 0.8 band.

Table 4 confirms AW beats BC in all eight settings and beats both BC and Forced CHECK in five, not all eight. The primary training objective is terminal task-rubric reward only; HMS is post-hoc. The released epsilon-perturbed behavior law has reconstructable propensities under a pinned code/config/mask, but trajectory records do not log epsilon, policy version, legal-action mask or mu(a|s). The paper does not report IPS/DR/TDR/FQE OPE; that is a proposed extension, not source evidence.

Shekhar's universal composite e-process is first-order alpha→0 optimal, not finite-deadline optimal. Clerico et al.'s arbitrary-e-process equivalence is simple-vs-simple, so the worker's composite matched-pair Bellman claim is only within its declared sign-betting class. The conditional sign e-factor identity, KT nuisance factorization/R_rho=0.111391 at n=50,d=20, and exact full-KT/sign-Jeffreys/GRO crossing probabilities at T=10/20/30/50 were independently recomputed and match the worker; the numerical Bellman power grid was not independently rerun.

FailFast Tables 3/6 and Atomix RQ1/RQ3/joint-stress values are verified. Table 6 Wait-vs-Immediate has no dedicated reported CI/significance test, so it supports a cut-timing module by point estimate but not a statistically established causal contradiction. Atomix's full-pool p≈0.50 Fisher test pools 38 tasks × 3 trials; no task-clustered/hierarchical equivalence analysis is reported. RQ3 zero leakage is also achieved by fully wired TCC-Confirm and Mutex+WAL+Rollback, so that axis is not unique to Tx-Full.
